strengths: The paper presents a unified, mathematically principled Product of Experts (PoE) framework that successfully integrates heterogeneous generative models, discriminative rewards, and physics-based simulators without requiring retraining.

The proposed sampling framework relies on a combination of Annealed Importance Sampling (AIS) and Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) to tackle the low acceptance rate problem of naive rejection sampling in high-dimensional visual spaces.

The approach is demonstrated across multiple diverse and challenging tasks, including graphics-engine-instructed image editing, physics-simulator-guided video generation, and regional layout-based text-to-image synthesis, showcasing its flexibility.
Quantitative and qualitative results consistently outperform strong baselines, demonstrating both superior controllability and high visual quality.
The manuscript is well-written, with clear mathematical formulations and detailed explanations of the implementations.
weaknesses: The main limitation is the high computational cost of the sampling process at inference time. As noted in Appendix B, generating a single video can take up to 30 minutes on powerful H200 GPUs, which limits real-time usability.

The conditional sampling approximation introduced in Equation 7 relies on a heuristic penalty term with a hyperparameter (learning rate $w$). While empirical results show its effectiveness, a deeper theoretical justification or analysis of its impact on the target distribution is somewhat lacking.

The scalability of the proposed SMC/AIS framework to a larger number of experts (e.g., more than three or four simultaneous experts) is not thoroughly investigated, leaving it unclear how the sampling efficiency scales as constraints accumulate.

strengths: Formulates visual generation tasks under heterogeneous constraints in a unified, training-free Product of Experts framework, bridging diffusion/flow generative priors, discriminative rewards, and physical simulators.

Proposes an effective sampling scheme leveraging Annealed Importance Sampling (AIS) and Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) that only requires black-box access to the discriminative experts, bypassing the need for dense, differentiable gradients.
Introduces conditional generative experts via flow-field modifications to handle the spatial/temporal dependencies between different regions, reducing multi-modality conflicts.

Demonstrates versatile applications with impressive results across graphics-engine image editing, physics-simulator video generation, and regional text-to-image composition, outperforming several competitive baselines.
weaknesses: High computational cost at inference time: generating a single sample takes between 4 and 30 minutes on H200 GPUs due to the MCMC steps and particle filtering, which limits the real-time applicability of the method.

The evaluation datasets are relatively small (e.g., 30 scenes for image insertion, 12-21 scenes for simulator-guided video generation), which makes the quantitative analysis somewhat limited in scale.
The regional composition heavily depends on an external LLM layout generator; the robustness of the PoE composition to inaccurate or suboptimal layouts is not thoroughly explored.

The approximation of discriminative scores using the predicted endpoint (r_t(x) ≈ r(x_hat)) is crucial but might be unstable in early sampling stages (large t) when the predicted endpoint contains significant noise.

strengths: Strong motivation and elegant conceptual framework: Composing heterogeneous experts (such as different generative priors, discriminative VLMs, and physical simulators) at inference time without retraining is a highly practical and promising direction.

Solid probabilistic foundation: Utilizing Annealed Importance Sampling (AIS) and Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) to address the vanishing acceptance rate of naive rejection sampling is mathematically sound and well-suited for high-dimensional visual spaces.

Demonstrated versatility: The framework is evaluated across several distinct, complex tasks (graphics-engine-instructed image editing, simulator-guided video generation, and regional text-to-image composition), showing its general applicability.
High-quality visual results: The quantitative and qualitative results indicate a clear improvement in controllability and instruction-following compared to monolithic baselines.
weaknesses: Extremely high computational cost and inference latency: As detailed in the discussion (Appendix B), generating a single sample takes 4 to 30 minutes on state-of-the-art hardware (NVIDIA H200 GPUs). This severe bottleneck limits the practical utility of the proposed method for real-world or interactive scenarios.

Small-scale evaluation: The quantitative evaluations are performed on very small datasets (e.g., 30 scenes in Section 4.2 and 12-21 scenes in Section 4.3). A larger-scale benchmark would provide much more robust evidence of the method's reliability and generalizability.

Complex multi-model dependency: The pipeline relies heavily on orchestrating multiple massive pre-trained models (FLUX.1, Wan2.1, VQAScore, GPT-4o, etc.). This makes reproduction, debugging, and deployment highly complex and sensitive to the constituent models' behaviors.
Lack of core details in the main text: Crucial approximations such as the conditional sampling formulation (Eq. 7) are relegated to the appendix without much intuitive explanation in the main text.

strengths: Principled Formulation: Formulating controllable image and video generation under a unified Product-of-Experts (PoE) framework is theoretically elegant and conceptually clean, allowing the seamless combination of heterogeneous models (diffusion/flow-based, autoregressive, VLMs, and physics constraints) without any training.

Improved Sampling Efficiency: By combining Annealed Importance Sampling (AIS) with Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) resampling, the paper elegantly resolves the path-wise weight degeneracy issue common in prior sequential importance sampling schemes.

Impressive Versatility and Performance: The proposed framework is evaluated across multiple diverse and challenging tasks (graphics-engine-instructed image editing, character insertion, physics-guided video generation, and layout-controlled text-to-image). It outperforms strong, task-specific baselines both quantitatively and qualitatively.

Detailed and Honest Ablations: The paper provides thorough ablation studies, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed conditional sampling strategy (Table 1) and the benefits of SMC resampling under varying particle counts (Table 3 & Table 4).
weaknesses: High Computational Overhead: The primary bottleneck of the proposed method is its inference-time computational cost. Running 28–30 steps of MCMC/annealing with multiple particles takes around 4 minutes for images and 5–30 minutes for videos on high-end H200 GPUs. This restricts its utility for real-time or interactive applications, and a discussion on potential speedups (such as consistency models or distillation) is missing.

Slight Unclarity in Technical Details: In Eq. (6), the use of a `stopgrad` operator is introduced without a rigorous mathematical explanation of how it fits into the probabilistic or score-matching formulation. Additionally, in Algorithm 1, Line 10, the definition of $r_t^{(j)}(x^{(l)})$ is not explicitly detailed in the algorithm caption or step-by-step description.

Hyperparameter Sensitivity: The framework introduces several sensitive hyperparameters, such as the alignment weight $w$ in Eq. (6), the Langevin dynamics noise scale $\kappa$, and the annealing schedule $\xi$. It remains unclear how robust the system is to these hyperparameters or how easily they can be tuned when changing model backbones.

strengths: Unified and flexible probabilistic framework (Product-of-Experts) that allows composing heterogeneous models (flow/diffusion, autoregressive, and discriminative) at inference time without training.

Strong and diverse experimental validation across multiple tasks, including graphics-engine-instructed image editing, physics-simulator-guided video generation, and layout-controlled text-to-image generation.
Comprehensive qualitative results showing excellent adherence to complex constraints, spatial layout, and physical realism.
Well-written manuscript with detailed mathematical formulations in both the main body and the appendix.
weaknesses: Extreme computational overhead and inference latency: As detailed in the appendix, generating a single image takes ~4 minutes on an NVIDIA H200 GPU, and video generation takes up to 30 minutes on two H200 GPUs. This extreme latency severely limits the practical utility of the proposed method in real-world interactive scenarios.

Heavy reliance on a large number of particles (L) to achieve high performance, as shown in the ablation studies. This scales the computational cost and GPU memory usage linearly with L, making the approach highly resource-intensive.

The theoretical justification for the conditional sampling approximation (Equation 6 and Section C.3) is somewhat heuristic and relies on hand-wavy assumptions, such as assuming parent regions are conditionally independent and representing the deviation of flow vectors with a simple Gaussian distribution.

Incremental algorithmic novelty: Composing generative models and steering them with discriminative rewards using SMC or MCMC has been explored in several recent works (e.g., Skreta et al., 2025; He et al., 2025; Du et al., 2023). The integration of AIS and SMC here is a natural extension rather than a fundamental algorithmic breakthrough.

The evaluation datasets are relatively small in size (e.g., 30 scenes for image editing, 12 scenes for object-centric simulation), which makes it difficult to fully assess the robustness and generalizability of the proposed sampling method across highly diverse scenarios.

strengths: Presents a mathematically rigorous and unified Product-of-Experts (PoE) framework that successfully integrates heterogeneous generative models (flow-based and autoregressive), discriminative models (VLMs), and rule-based physics simulators at inference time without requiring retraining.

Introduces an elegant sampling algorithm combining Annealed Importance Sampling (AIS) and Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) that avoids the weight degeneracy problems of path-wise importance weights by utilizing per-timestep MCMC kernels.

Demonstrates impressive versatility across multiple complex visual generation tasks, including graphics-engine-directed image editing, physics-simulator-instructed video generation, and layout-controlled text-to-image generation.

Provides thorough quantitative and qualitative results, outperforming strong baselines (e.g., Magic Insert, 3DIS-FLUX, RF-Solver) across a wide range of metrics, along with clear ablation studies on key components like conditional sampling and SMC resampling.
weaknesses: Significant computational overhead: Generating a single sample requires 4 minutes for images and up to 30 minutes for autoregressive video models, which limits real-world, interactive applications.

The conditional sampling approximation in Equation (6) relies on several heuristic assumptions (e.g., conditional independence and Gaussian deviations of flow predictions), and the framework's sensitivity to the hyperparameter $w$ is not thoroughly analyzed.
The setup complexity is relatively high, requiring task-specific selection and manual engineering/tuning of different expert configurations for each application.
